THE ESSENTIALS

What is a Registered Agent?

Every US state legally requires LLCs and Corporations to designate and maintain a Registered Agent. This agent is responsible for receiving official notices, state tax documents, and legal process (like lawsuit summons) on behalf of the business.

For international founders, a professional Registered Agent is the critical bridge connecting your foreign operation to US legal infrastructure. We provide the mandatory physical street address in the state of formation and ensure all official mail is digitized and forwarded to you immediately.

Core Responsibilities

  • **Legal Mail Receipt:** Accepting Service of Process during business hours.
  • **State Compliance:** Forwarding annual report reminders and tax notices.
  • **Privacy Shield:** Using our address on public records instead of yours.
THE RISK

The Danger of Non-Compliance

Losing your Registered Agent puts your entire corporate structure at immediate risk.

Administrative Dissolution

If the state cannot reach your business due to an invalid Registered Agent, they will revoke your company's good standing and dissolve the entity, erasing your liability protection.

Default Judgments

If your business is sued and there is no agent to receive the summons, you may lose the case by default without even knowing you were being sued.

Loss of Privacy

Attempting to use your own personal or virtual address as your Registered Agent address makes it permanent public record, exposing you to junk mail and direct legal service.

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

A Registered Agent is an individual or business entity designated to receive official legal and tax correspondence on behalf of a company. Every state requires you to maintain a Registered Agent who is a resident of that state or a corporation authorized to do business there.

Yes. Your Registered Agent must have a physical street address (not a P.O. Box) in the state where your LLC or Corporation is formed.

Failing to maintain a Registered Agent can result in your company losing its 'good standing' with the state. This can lead to administrative dissolution, meaning your company is effectively shut down by the state, and you lose limited liability protection.

Yes, if you reside in the state where your company is formed, you can be your own Registered Agent. However, this means your home address becomes public record, and you must be available during normal business hours to receive service of process.

Using a professional Registered Agent protects your privacy (keeping your personal address off public records), ensures you never miss critical legal documents if you're traveling, and provides a professional front for your business.

Service of process is the legal term for the delivery of legal documents, such as a summons or subpoena, when a business is sued or summoned to court.

We scan all official state and legal documents received on your behalf and upload them to a secure portal, notifying you immediately via email so you never miss a deadline.

Absolutely. Our Registered Agent service is perfect for non-US residents who need a physical US presence and a reliable way to receive official state and IRS correspondence.

A Registered Agent address is strictly for legal and state documents. If you need a general business mailing address for customer returns, bank statements, or Amazon, you would need a separate Virtual Mailbox service.

Registered Agent services are typically billed annually. Our transparent pricing means you pay a flat $99/year to maintain compliance.

We primarily provide Registered Agent services in Wyoming for our international clients, as it's the most popular state for non-US resident LLC formation.
